artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a real semisimple Lie group acting on a period (classifying) domain D for polarized Hodge structures of fixed type, realized as an open G-orbit in the compact dual flag variety, and let H denote the complex upper half-plane. A holomorphic map Φ : H → D is called horizontal if its differential at every point takes values in the horizontal tangent subbundle of D (the subbundle imposed by Griffiths transversality).

Suppose Φ : H → D is a horizontal holomorphic map satisfying the equivariance relation
   Φ(z + 1) = Φ(z) · T  for all z ∈ H,
where T ∈ G is an element of infinite order which preserves an integral lattice (so that T is an "integral" element of G).

Assume that as Im(z) → ∞, the image Φ(z) converges to a boundary point Ω₀ lying on the boundary of D in the compact dual. Let B(Ω₀) ⊂ G denote the parabolic subgroup of G stabilizing Ω₀, and let R_u(B(Ω₀)) denote its unipotent radical.

Prove or disprove: there exists a positive integer N such that T^N ∈ R_u(B(Ω₀)).
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is essentially the local monodromy theorem for variations of Hodge structure: monodromy around a puncture is quasi-unipotent, and a power lies in the unipotent radical of the parabolic stabilizer of the limiting Hodge filtration. Quasi-unipotency was proved by Borel and Landman, and the full statement (a power of T lies in the unipotent radical of the parabolic stabilizing the limit point) is a consequence of Schmid's Nilpotent Orbit Theorem and SL₂-orbit theorem (Schmid, Invent. Math. 1973). The conjecture is therefore considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Variation of Hodge structure: The singularities of the period mapping (Schmid)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the Nilpotent Orbit Theorem and SL₂-orbit theorem, proving that the monodromy is quasi-unipotent and a power lies in the unipotent radical of the parabolic subgroup stabilizing the limiting filtration.

status_evidence.title: The nilpotent orbit theorem, old and new (Schnell)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Schmid's nilpotent orbit theorem describing the limiting behavior of period maps and the unipotent structure of monodromy.
status_evidence.claim: Reaffirms that Schmid's theorem settles the conjecture.
